clue.text: Where guitarist might pause to view navel area?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a pause halfway through a guitar phrase or lick comes in the middle of a riff
the belly region of the body between chest and waist

explanation.surface: A rock guitarist stops mid-song to admire someone's exposed belly button.
explanation.definitionFit: The stomach region around the belly button is the part of the torso called this.

clue.text: US city not entirely accepting south has a rotten atmosphere

indicators.note: the shortened city takes the abbreviation for south into itself
the city's name is not given in full, losing its final letter

parts.note: Miami is a city in Florida
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: An American city has a foul, polluted air about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims MIAMI to MIAM; 'accepting' puts S inside to make MIASM, then A is added; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious vapour, an unhealthy or putrid smell hanging in the air.

clue.text: Guts, or heart lost in loved one

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for a loved one is dropped

parts.note: a darling is someone dear to you

explanation.surface: Someone's courage, or their spirit, has gone missing over a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart lost' removes the middle L of DARLING; 'or' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts in the sense of courage or nerve is boldness, a synonym of the noun form.

clue.text: State must block Venetian play, whatever happens

indicators.note: the state abbreviation has to sit inside and obstruct the other letters
the letters of the word Venetian are set in play, mixed freely

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York state

explanation.surface: A state authority has to stop a Venetian theatre production regardless of anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a stage drama but is the anagram signal, giving INAEVENT; 'must block' sets the state inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning regardless, no matter what occurs.

clue.text: Refuse to take line into attack, heading for home

indicators.note: the line letter goes inside the word for attack

parts.note: a fit is an attack or seizure of illness

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, of the word home is taken

explanation.surface: Someone declines to join a battle line, preferring to make for home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun (rubbish).
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun means rubbish or dirt, and filth is foul waste matter.

clue.text: See 28
Bringing off crime, saint not I?

definitions.text: Bringing off crime, saint not I?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are let off their order and reorganised, minus the named letter

parts.note: the letter I is the part excluded, as the clue says 'not I'

explanation.surface: Someone accomplishing a crime protests that they are no saint, are they?
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' tells you to take I out: CRIME SAINT less I rearranges to the answer. The whole clue also describes the villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer pulling off a crime, certainly no saint, is a villain or scoundrel.

clue.text: It's the whole thing, you fool!

parts.note: U is text-speak shorthand for you
a nit is a silly person, a nitwit

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that it's everything, calling their friend an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single complete entity, one whole thing regarded as an individual.

clue.text: Poet's written about English medical graduate

indicators.note: the poet's name is written around the extra letter

parts.note: A. E. Housman was the poet of A Shropshire Lad; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A poet has written about an English doctor fresh from medical school.
explanation.walkthrough: A houseman is the British term for a newly qualified hospital doctor, an intern.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior hospital doctor just out of medical school is known in Britain by this title.

clue.text: Pilfer your secret

parts.note: to pilfer is to steal
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: An order to lift something you have hidden away.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means furtive or done in secret so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Not viewing odds, favour a team which is close to one's heart

definitions.text: which is close to one's heart

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are ignored and only the even ones are seen

explanation.surface: Someone ignores the betting odds and backs a team they hold dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to one's heart' looks figurative, but it is literal: the great artery leaves the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart, so it is physically right next to it.

clue.text: Roughly speaking, was it the on-screen bone that ___, showing exhaustion?

indicators.note: the words are only approximately as pronounced, a rough sound-alike

parts.words: was it the on-screen bone that ___
parts.note: the film collie Lassie fills the screen role, and what a dog does to a bone is chewed, so the gap is Lassie chewed

explanation.surface: A question about whether the screen dog was the one gnawing a bone till worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: Lassie is the famous collie of film and television; 'Lassie chewed', said roughly, gives the word; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is weariness, a state of physical or mental tiredness and lack of energy.

clue.text: See 28
Circus performer shut up

definitions.meaning: a performing marine mammal balancing balls in a circus
to close tightly, as an envelope or a jar

explanation.definitionFit: A seal is a performing animal in circuses, and to seal is to close something up tight.

clue.text: Empty vehicle needing fresh oil, in power it's flown

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for power

parts.note: might means power or strength

indicators.note: the vehicle word loses its inside, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the letters of oil are freshly rearranged

explanation.surface: An empty car needs new oil to get its power back, but this one flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' strips the middle of the vehicle and 'fresh' scrambles the oil; 'in' sets both after the first two letters of the power word. 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A microlight is a very small, light aircraft, so it is something that is flown.

clue.text: Italian flight cut, can I change? Might this have stopped you?

indicators.note: the Italian word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: volo is Italian for a flight
change in the pocket is cash

explanation.surface: An Italian flight is cancelled and a passenger asks about changing plans.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the 2010 Icelandic eruption that grounded European air travel; 'change' looks like a verb but is coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Volcanic ash clouds ground aircraft, as in 2010, so it might have halted your journey.

clue.text: New sale man backed up over crumbling property under contract

indicators.note: the letters of sale are made new, rearranged
in a down entry the pronoun is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
something crumbling is old and decaying

explanation.surface: A new sale agent reverses his position on a run-down property he has contracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' gives LEAS from SALE; 'backed up' turns HE to EH; 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasehold property is held under a lease, a contract for a fixed term rather than owned outright.

clue.text: Force of nature brought to skin of frog, stuffing a fish

indicators.note: the pieces are stuffed inside the fish

parts.note: cod is a fish
taken as written

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word frog, its skin

explanation.surface: A bizarre recipe: frog's skin stuffed inside a fish, a natural force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought' is a link; the A comes first in the answer although it sits later in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of God is the legal term for a natural disaster beyond human control.

clue.text: Those looking to dress king in the emperor's new clothes?

indicators.note: the starers wrap around the king letter like clothing

parts.note: starers are people who stare
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Onlookers try to clothe the king in the fairy tale's invisible new outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Starkers is British slang for stark naked; the emperor in the fairy tale wore nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor's new clothes did not exist, so wearing them means being completely naked.

clue.text: Plant needing shade put in vessel

indicators.note: the shade goes inside the vessel

parts.note: a coaster is a coastal trading ship
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A gardener says a plant needs shade when placed in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks like a plant pot, but it is a coaster, a ship; 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotoneaster is a shrub with red berries, a common garden plant.

clue.text: Get on with leading empire

parts.note: to do, as in how are you doing, is to get on
main means chief or leading

explanation.surface: An instruction to make progress while heading an empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a realm or territory ruled by one sovereign, as an empire is.

clue.text: Break for depression

definitions.meaning: a pause or holiday period, as for parliament or school
an alcove or hollow set back in a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A recess is both an interval in business and a hollowed niche or indentation.

clue.text: Found in book, rare edible plant

indicators.note: the letters are found running inside these words

explanation.surface: A rare edible plant is discovered in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra, also called ladies' fingers, is a vegetable plant with edible pods.

clue.text: Workers carry around a link, regularly, as record filed away?

parts.note: men are workers, a workforce

indicators.note: the carrying word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to tote is to carry

indicators.note: every other letter of link is taken

explanation.surface: Labourers ferry a connecting part about, to be logged in the files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the first and third letters of link; with A they sit inside the carrying word just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mental note is a reminder kept in memory, a record filed away in the head.

clue.text: Speedy boat turned up having caught nothing

indicators.note: the reversed boat catches the extra letter inside it
in a down entry the boat is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat
O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A fast boat capsized after catching nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: TON-UP is British slang for doing 100 mph on a motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton-up describes going at a hundred miles an hour, hence very fast.

clue.text: See 28
Politician, one blasted as rookie

parts.note: a Green is a member of the Green Party
a horn is blasted when it is blown

explanation.surface: A politician is attacked for being a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasted' looks like criticism; it is a horn being sounded. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is an inexperienced newcomer, a novice.

clue.text: Serious plot

definitions.meaning: a burial place in a cemetery

explanation.surface: A conspiracy that is no laughing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave means solemn, and a grave is a burial plot in a graveyard.

clue.text: Treated with contempt, university squeezed, then abandoned

indicators.note: the university letter is squeezed into the slang word

parts.note: dissed is slang for disrespected

explanation.surface: A university was insulted, squeezed financially, and finally left to decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Disused means no longer in use, abandoned or left idle.

clue.text: To support what one's said, eat bread or suck lolly?

definitions.meaning: to back up ... words with action or a stake
bread and lolly are slang for cash, so eating or sucking them puts cash in the mouth

annotation.spelling: PUT ONE'S MONEY WHERE ONE'S MOUTH IS

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means backing one's claims with action, and literally bread and lolly are slang for cash being eaten.
